en.t: so that outsiders will not become suspicious.”

units.source_text: 源氏看见她面有不快之色，答道：“如此说来，我该走了。”

en.t: Genji saw displeasure on her face and answered, “If that is how it is, I should leave.”
He then stepped outside the gate.

units.source_text: 忽闻东院花散里那边传来筝笛合奏之声，音节美妙悦耳。

en.t: Suddenly he heard the sound of koto and flute playing together from Lady Hanachirusato’s quarters in the eastern wing, their notes beautiful and pleasing to the ear.

units.source_text: 这是夕雾中将和一向时刻不离的几个游伴正在奏乐。

en.t: It was Lieutenant General Yugiri and several companions who were always at his side making music.

units.source_text: 源氏说：“吹笛的想必是柏木头中将，吹得真好极了！”

en.t: Genji said, “The one playing the flute must be Kashiwagi, the Captain Secretary. How wonderfully he plays!”

units.source_text: 他又不想回去了，便派人前去转告夕雾：“这里篝火的光很凉爽，把我留住了。”

en.t: No longer wishing to go back, he sent someone to tell Yugiri, “The cool light of the bonfire here has kept me from leaving.”

units.source_text: 夕雾立刻偕柏木头中将及弁少将三人联袂而来。

en.t: Yugiri immediately came together with Kashiwagi, the Captain Secretary, and Ben no Shosho, the three arriving side by side.

units.source_text: 源氏对他们说：“我听了笛中吹出的秋风乐，不胜哀愁之感呢。”

en.t: Genji said to them, “Hearing the autumn wind music breathed through the flute fills me with unbearable melancholy.”

units.source_text: 就取过琴来，略弹一节，亲切可爱。

en.t: He then took up the koto and played a brief passage, intimate and charming.

units.source_text: 夕雾在笛上吹出南吕调，音节十分优美。

en.t: Yugiri played the Nanryo mode on the flute, and the notes were exceedingly graceful.

units.source_text: 柏木心里想着玉鬘，歌声迟迟不能出口。

en.t: Kashiwagi was thinking of Tamakazura, and for a long while his singing voice would not come forth.

units.source_text: 柏木的弟弟弁少将便打起拍子来，低声吟唱，其音酷似金钟儿的鸣声。

en.t: Kashiwagi’s younger brother, Ben no Shosho, began beating time and chanted softly, his voice closely resembling the cry of a bell cricket.

units.source_text: 源氏和着琴声唱了两遍，便把琴让与柏木。

en.t: Genji sang twice to the sound of the koto, then handed the instrument over to Kashiwagi.

units.source_text: 柏木弹的爪音，华丽而优美，技法不亚于他的父亲内大臣。

en.t: The tones Kashiwagi drew from the strings with his fingertips were splendid and graceful, and his technique was no less fine than that of his father, the Minister of the Center.
